messages:
sara.p: FYI customer 'acme-corp' reported ~800 objects that were supposed to be removed during last week's retention cutover but are still searchable via the embeddings API and internal search. They provided delete API timestamps and we have matching audit-log entries. They need an auditor-friendly timeline and immediate remediation.
ops-bot: incident-bot: New escalation created: retention-search-leak for tenant acme-corp. Priority: high. Assigned to support oncall.
raj.k: Can you drop the tenant id + 3 sample object ids and a trace id from the customer's delete request? Also paste the delete API call (cURL) if available.
sara.p: tenant: acme-corp-556
object ids: obj_8b3f, obj_d9a2, obj_1f7c
trace_id: trace-20260308-9f3c
cURL the customer sent:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/objects/delete \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -d '{"tenant":"acme-corp-556","objects":["obj_8b3f","obj_d9a2","obj_1f7c"]}'
```
emily.sre: quick hypotheses: 1) search index didn't receive tombstone updates during cutover 2) expunge worker errored (KMS decrypt) and left tombstoned objects in storage but not purged 3) backfill job rehydrated older objects with an older KMS key header. Can someone grep the expunge logs around trace-20260308-9f3c?
raj.k: I pulled logs: deletion_worker shows these errors around the trace:
```
ERROR deletion_worker: expunge failed object=obj_8b3f err="kms: decrypt failed: key-version-mismatch" retrying
INFO deletion_worker: queued for retry after 30s
```
Also noticed object metadata header enc-key-v: v2 for some objects and v1 for others.
akshay.privacy: that key-version mismatch is worrying for compliance. If expunge retried but never succeeded, objects would remain readable (if storage layer still returns encrypted blob and we decrypt for search). Do we know whether search path uses service-side decrypt or a cached plaintext index? Need to confirm whether search hits are returning content or embedding ID only.
emily.sre: Search reads use the index (plaintext tokens) and embeddings store can fallback to decrypt-at-read for on-demand. If index still contains content, users can search even if expunge failed. Check search-index timestamp for those doc ids and deletion flags in the index.
raj.k: Running quick queries now: `SELECT deleted_at, tombstoned, index_updated_at FROM objects WHERE id IN ('obj_8b3f','obj_d9a2','obj_1f7c');` Results: deleted_at set, tombstoned = true, index_updated_at = '2026-03-08T12:03:22Z' but index commit later was '2026-03-08T12:05:40Z' with no tombstone diff applied. Looks like index commit missed tombstone delta during the cutover window.
sara.p: Customer says they didn't see errors in client-side responses — delete API returned 200. They want confirmation that the objects will be completely removed from search and storage. Legal is starting to ask for a signed timeline.
lisa.legal: If the customer requests a signed attestation we need an internal timeline and explanation. Please include whether data was still retrievable via API/search and exact times when it was accessible. Also confirm if any other customers are impacted.
akshay.privacy: Action: run a targeted expunge job (emergency) for tenant acme-corp-556 that ignores KMS key-version mismatch by using the current key mapping and forcing rewrap before final delete. Need KMS team's ok. Also we must snapshot audit logs before making any emergency changes.
emily.sre: Proposed mitigation steps:
- 1) Block search index reads for acme-corp (switch read-route to deny) — short term
- 2) Snapshot audit logs + object headers (store in retention-incident bucket)
- 3) Run targeted expunge with additional logging and backoff disabled for those object ids
- 4) Rebuild index deltas post-expunge and verify no hit for sample queries
I'll prepare the job and change plan.
raj.k: I need permission to run expunge (sensitive). @akshay.privacy @lisa.legal can you approve emergency expunge for acme-corp-556 now? We will tag everything in incidents channel and include the audit snapshot.
akshay.privacy: Approved for emergency expunge on those sample objects and tenant-scoped run. Legal sign-off required for broader bucket expunge — we can proceed on targeted IDs.
lisa.legal: Approve targeted expunge for the listed object ids and any associated replicas. For a tenant-wide purge we need COE sign-off. Please produce timeline within 4 hours.
sara.p: ack. Assigning to @raj.k for the run and @emily.sre to perform index block + verify. I'll notify customer that we are running an emergency remediation and will provide timeline in 4 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ops-bot: deploy-bot: retention-expunge-job scheduled: job_id=expunge-20260310-001 owner=raj.k eta=10m
raj.k: Starting the expunge now. Will paste logs and final verification in this thread. If anything surfaces that requires rolling back, i'll post immediately.
sara.p: thanks team. Please also include whether this is systemic (cutover pipeline bug) or an isolated KMS metadata mismatch. We need a postmortem if systemic.
emily.sre: noted — I'll triage index pipeline for the cutover window and report findings in incidents/retention-cutover.
raj.k: initial run finished for sample ids: obj_8b3f,obj_d9a2,obj_1f7c — expunge returned success, no decrypt error this run (used rewrap path). Verified search: `search("some unique phrase from obj_8b3f")` returns 0 hits. Audit snapshot saved at s3://retention-incident/acme-corp-556/2026-03-10-logs.tar.gz
sara.p: passing to customer with timeline and artifacts. will follow up here with their confirmation. Closing internal high-priority action until we verify if more objects require the same path. :white_check_mark:
